podcast_cover.name: title-first editorial cover
podcast_cover.mechanic: one strong title hierarchy with one calm brand field
podcast_cover.why: Best when the show name or episode title needs to read instantly at thumbnail size.
push: one portrait or product accent if explicitly supplied

podcast_cover.name: brand-field promo banner
podcast_cover.mechanic: one central copy block with one support motif
podcast_cover.why: Best when the asset should work across YouTube, social, and landing-page promo slots.
push: host or guest framing if supplied

podcast_banner.name: title-first editorial cover
podcast_banner.mechanic: one strong title hierarchy with one calm brand field
podcast_banner.why: Best when the show name or episode title needs to read instantly at thumbnail size.
push: one portrait or product accent if explicitly supplied

podcast_banner.name: brand-field promo banner
podcast_banner.mechanic: one central copy block with one support motif
podcast_banner.why: Best when the asset should work across YouTube, social, and landing-page promo slots.
push: host or guest framing if supplied

pattern_system.name: banded route lattice
pattern_system.why: Best when the brand should feel systemic, infrastructural, and modular without becoming abstract slop.

pattern_system.name: pillar fragment grid
pattern_system.why: Best when you want the mark to feel editorial and architectural with tighter module discipline.

pattern_system.name: carrier field system
pattern_system.why: Best when the system should branch easily into posters, stickers, and product accents later.

sticker_family.name: carrier repetition
sticker_family.why: Best when you want the family to feel unmistakably branded and easy to deploy as merch or social accents.

sticker_family.name: utility badge family
sticker_family.why: Best when you want a more functional, product-adjacent sticker set with tight system coherence.

sticker_family.name: capsule strip set
sticker_family.why: Best when the brand should feel more collectible and motion-ready without losing discipline.

campaign_poster.name: single emblem field
campaign_poster.why: Best for bold poster framing with one commanding brand move.

campaign_poster.name: band strike poster
campaign_poster.why: Best when the brand should feel more active and infrastructural.

campaign_poster.name: quiet field with footer
campaign_poster.why: Best when you want more editorial restraint and premium calm.

brand_bumper.name: mask reveal
brand_bumper.why: Best when you want one elegant reveal and a clean final hold.

brand_bumper.name: band slide reveal
brand_bumper.why: Best when the identity should feel more infrastructural and system-led.

brand_bumper.name: edge crop settle
brand_bumper.why: Best when you want a calmer, more editorial motion signature.

brand_scene.name: architectural corridor
brand_scene.mechanic: deep perspective with brand mark at the vanishing point
brand_scene.why: Monumental hero moments. Use sparingly — easy to over-rely on.

brand_scene.name: aerial landscape
brand_scene.mechanic: bird-eye view of a terrain or cityscape with brand geometry embedded in the landscape
brand_scene.why: Conveys scale and network. Good for ecosystem/platform positioning.

brand_scene.name: material close-up
brand_scene.mechanic: extreme close-up of a textured surface — terracotta, woven lattice, stone carving — with brand geometry emerging from the material
brand_scene.why: Tactile and premium. Works well for backgrounds and texture fills.

brand_scene.name: abstract data flow
brand_scene.mechanic: flowing lines, particles, or light paths suggesting data movement through a governed system — routed through lattice structures
brand_scene.why: Communicates the protocol/network idea without showing literal UI.

brand_scene.name: still life / object composition
brand_scene.mechanic: carefully arranged objects on a warm surface — carved tokens, manuscript pages, architectural models — that suggest curation and governance
brand_scene.why: Editorial and intimate. Good for social and detail shots.

concept_illustration.name: abstract system diagram
concept_illustration.mechanic: flowing lines connecting nodes through governance gates — manifests entering, votes accumulating, approved updates emerging
concept_illustration.why: Explains the system visually without words.

concept_illustration.name: layered landscape
concept_illustration.mechanic: stratified horizontal layers suggesting library stacks, governance tiers, or distribution channels
concept_illustration.why: Good for conveying depth/layers of the protocol.

concept_illustration.name: single symbol expansion
concept_illustration.mechanic: the brand mark geometry exploded or expanded into a larger compositional system — columns becoming a forest, lattice becoming a city grid
concept_illustration.why: Shows the brand as a living system, not a static logo.

hero_banner.name: gradient atmosphere
hero_banner.mechanic: wide cinematic gradient with subtle brand geometry embedded as texture or particle field
hero_banner.why: Clean backdrop for overlaid text. Works as website hero.

hero_banner.name: split composition
hero_banner.mechanic: asymmetric split — one side dense with brand texture/pattern, other side open negative space for text overlay
hero_banner.why: Practical for hero with text overlay on one side.

social.name: proof showcase
social.mechanic: one real product surface or artifact displayed on a warm brand background
social.why: Best for announcing specific features or content.

social.name: typography-led
social.mechanic: bold headline on a textured brand background — the copy IS the visual
social.why: Best for provocative statements, quotes, or announcements. Use HTML backend for exact fonts.

social.name: ambient brand
social.mechanic: close-up brand texture or pattern with a subtle mark presence — no text, pure mood
social.why: Good for maintaining feed presence between announcements.

system_explainer_illustration.name: visible routing explainer
system_explainer_illustration.mechanic: one visible routed flow with gates, branches, or transforms
system_explainer_illustration.why: Best when the material should explain one concrete protocol or product mechanic in a SaaS-useful way.

system_explainer_illustration.name: parts-to-whole explainer
system_explainer_illustration.why: Best when the product truth is about components combining into one governed or routed system.
push: annotation-like clarity without actual UI chrome

editorial_metaphor_illustration.name: single symbolic scene
editorial_metaphor_illustration.mechanic: one dominant metaphor with one support cue maximum
editorial_metaphor_illustration.why: Best for essays, launch narratives, and thought pieces where one metaphor should carry the message.

editorial_metaphor_illustration.name: opener still
editorial_metaphor_illustration.mechanic: one still life or staged metaphor
editorial_metaphor_illustration.why: Best when the piece should feel like an editorial opener rather than a system diagram.

illustrated_brand_world.name: process-bearing world
illustrated_brand_world.mechanic: one environment that visibly implies work, ritual, or process
illustrated_brand_world.why: Best when explicit worldbuilding is desired but the brand's work still needs to feel present.

illustrated_brand_world.name: ritual environment
illustrated_brand_world.why: Best when the world should feel inhabited by the brand's philosophy, not just decorated with it.

proof_poster.name: quote-led proof poster
proof_poster.mechanic: quote or claim block supported by one proof payload
proof_poster.why: Best when a customer quote, statement, or campaign claim should lead while the brand mark stays secondary.

proof_poster.name: screenshot-led proof poster
proof_poster.mechanic: one screenshot or stat module as the main carrier
proof_poster.why: Best when the poster should feel grounded in product proof rather than abstract campaign energy.

site_pattern_tile.name: quiet deployable tile
site_pattern_tile.mechanic: one low-contrast repeat tile suitable for live UI backgrounds
site_pattern_tile.why: Best for production website surfaces where the pattern must support content rather than compete with it.

site_pattern_tile.name: section underlay system
site_pattern_tile.mechanic: one restrained underlay pattern with clear repeat grammar
site_pattern_tile.why: Best when you need a pattern that can stretch across pricing, docs, or feature sections without noise.

pattern_board.name: coherent variation board
pattern_board.mechanic: one repeat grammar expanded into a few related variants
pattern_board.why: Best for internal review when the team needs to inspect range without losing system coherence.

pattern_board.name: applications board
pattern_board.mechanic: one tile logic shown across a few support surfaces
pattern_board.why: Best when the goal is evaluating how one system behaves across backgrounds, borders, and cropped fields.

default_track.name: core brand extension
default_track.why: Best when you need a safe starting direction before branching.
